name.text: Interactive secant - drag A and B to a target average rate (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
A stone is thrown straight up. Its height above the ground after \(t\) seconds is \[ s(t) = {@v@}\,t - 5\,t^2 \text{ metres.} \]

The two points \(A\) and \(B\) sit on the curve. Dragging one moves it along the curve, choosing a start time \(a\) and an end time \(b\); the green line is the secant joining them, and its slope is the average rate of change \[ \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = \frac{s(b)-s(a)}{b-a}. \]

Drag \(A\) and \(B\) so that the average rate of change over \([a,\,b]\) equals \({@targ@}\) m/s. The live readout shows \(\Delta t\), \(\Delta s\) and the current average rate. There is more than one interval that works.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="ref_A" input-ref-ans2="ref_B" width='520px' height='430px']] var vv = {#v#}, tmax = {#float(tmax)#}, targ = {#targ#}; var Astart = {#float(a0)#}, Bstart = {#float(b0)#}; var s = function (t) { return vv * t - 5 * t * t; }; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-0.7, {#float(ytop)#}, tmax + 0.9, {#float(ybot)#}], keepAspectRatio: false, axis: true, grid: {majorStep: 1, minorStep: 0.5}, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}, defaultAxes: { x: {ticks: {insertTicks: false, ticksDistance: 1, minorticks: 4}, name: 't', withLabel: true, label: {position: 'rt', offset: [10, 12]}}, y: {ticks: {insertTicks: false, ticksDistance: 5, minorticks: 4}, name: 's', withLabel: true, label: {position: 'rt', offset: [12, 0]}} } }); // The stone's path (visible) and an invisible copy used as the rail. board.create('functiongraph', [s, 0, tmax], {strokeColor: '#0055bb', strokeWidth: 2.5, name: ''}); var rail = board.create('functiongraph', [s, 0, tmax], {visible: false}); board.create('text', [0.15, {#float(ytop-1.6)#}, 's(t) = ' + vv + 't − 5t²'], {color: '#0055bb', fontSize: 15, fixed: true}); // Draggable gliders on the curve. snapX keeps the x-coordinate on a 0.1 grid so // the exact target rate is reachable. var A = board.create('glider', [Astart, s(Astart), rail], { name: 'A', size: 5, strokeColor: '#1565c0', fillColor: '#1565c0', snapToGrid: false, snapX: 0.1, label: {offset: [-14, 10], color: '#1565c0', fontSize: 14} }); var B = board.create('glider', [Bstart, s(Bstart), rail], { name: 'B', size: 5, strokeColor: '#1565c0', fillColor: '#1565c0', snapToGrid: false, snapX: 0.1, label: {offset: [10, 10], color: '#1565c0', fontSize: 14} }); // Snap x to the nearest 0.1 after each drag (robust across JSXGraph builds). function snapGlider(P) { var xr = Math.round(P.X() * 10) / 10; if (xr < 0) { xr = 0; } if (xr > tmax) { xr = tmax; } P.setPositionDirectly(JXG.COORDS_BY_USER, [xr, s(xr)]); board.update(); } A.on('up', function () { snapGlider(A); }); B.on('up', function () { snapGlider(B); }); // Green secant (its slope IS the average rate). board.create('line', [A, B], {strokeColor: '#2e7d32', strokeWidth: 2.5, straightFirst: true, straightLast: true}); // Grey slope triangle: run Delta t and rise Delta s. var corner = function () { return [B.X(), A.Y()]; }; board.create('segment', [A, corner], {strokeColor: '#777', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2}); board.create('segment', [corner, B], {strokeColor: '#777', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2}); board.create('text', [function () { return (A.X() + B.X()) / 2; }, function () { return A.Y() - 1.4; }, function () { return 'Δt'; }], {color: '#555', fontSize: 13, fixed: true, anchorX: 'middle'}); board.create('text', [function () { return B.X() + 0.12; }, function () { return (A.Y() + B.Y()) / 2; }, function () { return 'Δs'; }], {color: '#555', fontSize: 13, fixed: true, anchorX: 'left'}); // Live readout: a, b, Δt, Δs and the average rate Δs/Δt (the secant slope). No // target-hit indicator, so the student judges for themselves whether they've met // the target rather than being told by a tick. Centred horizontally on the // parabola's axis of symmetry (t = v/10, the peak) and sitting just above the x-axis. var axisSym = vv / 10; // axis of symmetry / vertex of s(t) = v t - 5 t^2 board.create('text', [ axisSym, 0.4, function () { var a = A.X(), b = B.X(), sa = s(a), sb = s(b); var dt = b - a, ds = sb - sa; var rateTxt = Math.abs(dt) > 1e-6 ? '' + (ds / dt).toFixed(2) + ' m/s' : 'undefined (a = b)'; return '
' + 'a = ' + a.toFixed(1) + ' s,  b = ' + b.toFixed(1) + ' s
' + 'Δt = ' + dt.toFixed(1) + ' s,  ' + 'Δs = ' + ds.toFixed(1) + ' m
' + 'average rate = Δs/Δt = ' + rateTxt + '
'; } ], {useHTML: true, anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'bottom', fixed: true}); // Bind the two gliders to the hidden inputs: ans1 = [a, s(a)], ans2 = [b, s(b)]. stack_jxg.bind_point(ref_A, A); stack_jxg.bind_point(ref_B, B); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
The average rate of change of \(s(t) = {@v@}t - 5t^2\) over \([a,b]\) is the slope of the secant line: \[ \frac{s(b)-s(a)}{b-a}. \] For this parabola it works out to \({@v@} - 5(a+b)\), so any interval whose two times add up to \(a+b = \dfrac{{@v@}-({@targ@})}{5} = {@apb@}\) gives an average rate of \({@targ@}\) m/s. That is why more than one position of \(A\) and \(B\) scores full marks — for example \(a = {@a_ta@}\), \(b = {@b_ta@}\).

{@extranote@}

node.description: Degenerate check: are the two times the same (Delta t = 0)?

truefeedback.text: Right now \(A\) and \(B\) are at the same time, so \(\Delta t = 0\) and the average rate \(\dfrac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}\) is undefined. You need two different times: drag \(A\) and \(B\) apart so the interval \([a,b]\) has some width.

node.description: Property check: does the average rate equal the target?
Sign diagnostic: right magnitude but opposite sign (missed the negative)?

truefeedback.text: So close — your secant has the right steepness, but it slopes the wrong way. Its average rate is about \({@negtarg@}\) m/s, the opposite sign to the target \({@targ@}\) m/s. A rate is negative when the stone is falling (\(B\) lower than \(A\)), and positive when it is rising (\(B\) higher than \(A\)). To hit \({@targ@}\) m/s, {@signhint@}.

falsefeedback.text: Your interval has a valid width, but its average rate is not \({@targ@}\) m/s yet. The average rate is the slope of the green secant — tilt it by dragging \(A\) and \(B\) until the readout shows \({@targ@}\) m/s. Making the interval wider or narrower, or sliding it left or right, changes the slope.

qtest.description: Passing instance: the sample correct interval [a_ta, b_ta] hits the target.
A DIFFERENT valid interval also scores: a narrower interval with the same midpoint keeps a+b (hence the same average rate) and is always inside the domain.
Degenerate: A and B at the same time (a = b), Delta t = 0.
Wrong rate: a valid-width interval whose average rate is not the target (initial start positions).

Missed the negative: right magnitude, opposite sign (average rate = -targ). Meaningful only for a non-zero target - on a targ=0 variant there is no opposite sign, so run this against a non-zero-target seed.
